headline: Regional Lodging and Backcountry Permits
reservation: Accommodations in the Jackson Hole region, including glamping and cabins, frequently book a year in advance. Backcountry camping permits for the Teton Range are managed through a competitive reservation system on Recreation.gov. Always check the official NPS site for changing seasonal access and specific permit windows.

days.title: Valley Settlement History

stops.name: National Museum of Wildlife Art
stops.detail: View regional and international wildlife art overlooking the National Elk Refuge.

stops.name: Mormon Row
stops.detail: Walk among historic ranch structures with clear views of the mountain skyline.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; roads are well-maintained but wildlife sightings can cause delays.
days.note: The museum offers an indoor alternative if morning weather is unsettled.

days.title: Rivers and Ridges

stops.name: Snake River Overlook
stops.detail: Observe the famous view of the river winding toward the Tetons, popularized by Ansel Adams.

stops.name: Taggart Lake Trail
stops.detail: Hike a moderate loop through forest and meadow to reach the base of the mountains.

days.driving: Allow 1.5-2 hours; trailheads are popular and may require patience for parking.
days.note: Carry bear spray and know how to use it on all regional trails.

days.title: High Alpine Lakes

stops.name: Jackson Lake Shoreline
stops.detail: Visit the pebble beaches at Colter Bay for views across the park's largest body of water.

stops.name: Signal Mountain Summit Road
stops.detail: Drive the winding road for a panoramic view of the entire Jackson Hole valley.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; the road to Signal Mountain is narrow with sharp turns.
days.note: Check for seasonal road opening dates, as high-elevation routes open later in the spring.

intel.title: Regional Congestion
intel.text: Parking in the town of Jackson and at major park viewpoints is extremely limited during peak summer. Utilize public shuttles in Jackson where available to reduce traffic stress.

intel.title: Remote Areas
intel.text: Beyond the town of Jackson, signal strength drops rapidly. Do not rely on streaming GPS; use physical maps for navigating the Moose-Wilson corridor.

intel.title: Gateway Stations
intel.text: Jackson and Moose are the primary hubs for fuel and supplies. Ensure your tank is full before heading to remote areas like the Gros Ventre or northern park gates.

intel.title: Autumn Variations
intel.text: Fall foliage timing varies by year; cottonwoods usually turn in late September. Be prepared for early snow which can close roads temporarily.

intel.title: Waterway Permits
intel.text: All watercraft, including paddleboards, require a Wyoming AIS decal and a park-specific permit. Inspections are mandatory at designated stations before launching.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at JAC and stop in Jackson for supplies. Verify the specific food storage requirements for your regional lodging or campsite before unpacking.
plan.vehicle: An SUV is recommended for travelers planning to visit regional areas outside the main paved park loops; check for seasonal road closures.
plan.goldenHour: Snake River Overlook is a traditional sunset photography spot, with mountain shadows changing significantly as the sun drops.
